homonyms.basis: The census row carries no disambiguation field. The name names the collection (the address, the census's entity) and also the series in which it is published ('the now 86-volume work, The Oxyrhynchus Papyri', B2 F32) and the city where it was found; the research project of the same name is the subject of card 5 and of Wikipedia's external link (F37, F40). Each is a distinct entity beside the collection, never a sense of its name. No card is a homonym and T composes no other entity under the name; it composes one papyrus that is not of the collection (𝔓52, the Rylands fragment: CAP-1-03), recorded as outside the field, not as a homonym. 'POxy' and 'Oxyrhynchus Online' are the census's other names for the entity; oxyrhynchus.web.ox.ac.uk and www.papyrology.ox.ac.uk/POxy/ its hosts.

captures.description: THE OXYRHYNCHUS PAPYRI, BY NAME, ON GOOGLE'S AI OVERVIEW, SIGNED OUT, 2026-10-31: 'a massive collection of ancient manuscripts discovered in the garbage dumps of Oxyrhynchus (modern Bahnasa, Egypt) by Oxford classicists Bernard Grenfell and Arthur Hunt between 1896 and 1907.' The collection (EES, Oxford, 'an estimated 500,000 fragments'), the period, the languages, the content mix (90% documents, 10% literary and religious, 'early Christian gospels, and biblical fragments (such as Papyrus 52 and the Gospel of Thomas)'), the publication series. Seven cards: the collection's own Oxford page, Wikipedia, the EES, four videos.
